title: Data Representation
definition: Data representation is the chosen encoding through which values are stored, transmitted, or interpreted by a system.
purpose: Separate domain meaning from the concrete encoding used at a system boundary.
history: Computer systems use bounded numeric formats, character encodings, and interchange formats to represent information.
mental_model: The same meaning can travel in different containers, and the same visible symbols can be interpreted under different contracts.
analogy: A date can be written in several formats; the analogy fails because some encodings cannot preserve every possible source value.
common_mistakes: Assuming every numeric representation is exact
industry_notes: Interoperability depends on both sides agreeing on type, encoding, range, precision, and absence semantics.
ai_notes: Ask AI to state representation assumptions and produce boundary tests before accepting generated transformations.
interview_notes: Ask for examples where a representation preserves appearance but loses meaning, or preserves meaning with different bytes.
exercise_candidates: Compare text and numeric representations of identifiers
lab_candidates: Record representation risks in a conversion matrix
